questions.question: Before riding, a motorcycle operator should check the throttle. It should:
questions.explanation: Check your throttle and clutch before riding. The throttle should snap back when you release it. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: If a motorcycle rider takes a turn too fast, they may:

options.text: Have increased control of their motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause a rider to lose control. The motorcycle may cross into another lane or go off the road.

questions.question: The safest part of the lane:

options.text: Is always the left portion of the lane.
Is always the right portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: No single lane position is always safest. Adjust your position based on traffic, road conditions, and hazards.

questions.question: Pick a lane position that:

options.text: Hides you from other road users.
Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid hazards. Keep a safe space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: Mirrors on motorcycles:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Do not have blind spots because a motorcycle is usually smaller than a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has gone flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
A discharge of air can be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of your motorcycle may jerk or sway side to side. If you feel this movement, stop riding and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When cars are merging from an entrance ramp:

options.text: A motorcyclist should assume the entering drivers see them.
A motorcyclist should never assume the entering drivers see them.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should never assume the entering drivers see them.
questions.explanation: Give merging cars plenty of space and never assume drivers see you. Change lanes away from entering traffic if possible. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to allow safe merging.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the signal will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if safe. If you are already in the intersection, continue through.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Not make sudden movements, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make sudden movements, if possible.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake smoothly.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes because it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you.
Be comfortable and wear shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright clothes when riding to be more visible to other drivers.

questions.question: The best footwear for motorcyclists are:
questions.explanation: Leather boots give the best protection for your feet. Choose boots that are high and sturdy to support your ankles.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Always use both the front and rear brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: May be shared by the driver and passenger.
Are required for the driver and passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests for balance. Your motorcycle must have passenger footrests. This keeps your passenger from falling off and pulling you with them.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothes to be more visible when riding, even during the day. Reflective clothing also helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: As your motorcycle accelerates, you will need to:
questions.explanation: As you speed up, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle while carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes your motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing earlier when you have a passenger, reduce your speed, and look for larger gaps in traffic when merging or turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns drivers about a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns drivers that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is a major cause of many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern because the motorcycle has two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major cause of many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning the right braking technique is an important part of safe riding.

questions.question: What factors can affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Three major factors affect BAC: how much alcohol someone drinks, how fast they drink it, and their body weight.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider look for when choosing a protective jacket?

options.text: Made of leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket that covers your arms completely and fits snugly but allows you to move. Leather or strong synthetic materials with body armor offer the best protection.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Know what is happening both in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening both in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: Watch what is ahead of you, but also stay aware of what is behind you. Check your mirrors regularly to see what is happening behind you.

questions.question: What colors should motorcycle riders wear?
questions.explanation: Bright orange, red, yellow, and green colors help other drivers see motorcyclists on the road.

questions.question: If hazards are to your right, which side of your lane should you ride on?
questions.explanation: Position yourself to have the most space. If hazards are on your left, ride on the right side of your lane. If hazards are on your right, ride on the left side of your lane.
